{"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"You select MacroDroid features that will be needed to build a macro.

A MacroDroid macro is composed of three kinds of items:
- TRIGGERS: events that start the macro (e.g. TimeTrigger, BatteryLevelTrigger). Every macro has at least one trigger.
- ACTIONS: what the macro does when it runs (e.g. SendSmsAction, SetWifiAction).
- CONSTRAINTS: conditions that must be true for the macro/trigger/action to run (e.g. DeviceLockedConstraint, BatteryLevelConstraint).

Below is the full catalog of available features with a short description of each. This catalog is the ONLY source of valid names.

---
## TRIGGERS
- AccessibilityServiceStateTrigger: Triggers when accessibility service state changes
- ActivityRecognitionTrigger: Triggers based on detected user activity (walking, running, in vehicle, etc.)
- AirplaneModeTrigger: Triggers when airplane mode is enabled or disabled
- AndroidWearTrigger: Triggers from Android Wear/Wear OS events - app button press, watch connected, or watch disconnected
- AppActivityLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when a specific activity (screen) is launched or closed
- AppEnabledTrigger: Triggers when an application is enabled or disabled on the device
- ApplicationInstalledRemovedTrigger: Triggers when an application is installed, updated, or removed
- ApplicationLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when app is launched or closed. There is no separate AppCloseTrigger - use this trigger with m_launched=false to detect app close.
- AssistantActivatedTrigger: Triggers when the device's digital assistant (e.g. Gemini, Google Assistant, Bixby) opens or closes. Detects the assistant window appearing/disappearing - it cannot detect whether the assistant is actively listening. Useful for accessibility, e.g. playing a sound when the assistant opens for visually impaired users. Requires the accessibility service.
- AutoRotateChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-rotate setting changes
- AutoSyncChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-sync setting changes
- BatteryLevelTrigger: Triggers at specific battery level
- BatterySaverTrigger: Triggers when battery saver mode changes
- BatteryTemperatureTrigger: Triggers at specific battery temperature
- BluetoothBeaconTrigger: Triggers when Bluetooth beacon is detected
- BluetoothTrigger: Triggers on Bluetooth connection events
- BootTrigger: Triggers when device boots/restarts
- CalendarTrigger: Triggers based on calendar events
- CallActiveTrigger: Triggers when call becomes active (answered) - monitors both incoming and outgoing calls
- CallEndedTrigger: Triggers when a call ends
- CallMissedTrigger: Triggers when a call is missed. classType is "CallMissedTrigger" not "MissedCallTrigger".
- CameraFlashlightTrigger: Triggers when camera flashlight (torch) state changes
- CameraInUseTrigger: Triggers when camera starts or stops being used by another app
- CellConnectionTypeChangeTrigger: Triggers when the mobile (cellular) data connection type changes, e.g. LTE to 5G. Requires Android 11+. Magic text {cell_connection_type_new} (new) and {cell_connection_type_previous} (old) contain the fixed values 2G, 3G, LTE, 5G NSA, 5G SA or None. 5G NSA (non-standalone, 5G over an LTE core) is how most carriers deliver 5G; 5G SA is pure standalone 5G, so a macro that wants "any 5G" should enable both. None means no mobile data connection (e.g. airplane mode or no signal). Note the magic text value is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no mobile data connection)'. Requires phone state permission.
- CellTowerTrigger: Triggers when in/out of range of specified cell towers, or (anyCellChange=true) whenever the serving cell the phone is connected to changes. In anyCellChange mode no cell tower group is needed and magic text {cell_id_new} and {cell_id_previous} contain the new and previous cell IDs. Changes are not reported during calls or with no signal.
- ClipboardChangeTrigger: Triggers when clipboard content changes
- CustomSceneTrigger: Triggers when a custom scene is shown or dismissed (based on its identifier)
- DarkThemeTrigger: Triggers when dark theme is toggled
- DataOnOffTrigger: Triggers when overall data connectivity changes (WiFi OR mobile) - fires on connect/disconnect of any data connection, NOT specifically on mobile data being toggled
- DataUsedTrigger: Fires when cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period crosses (transitions from below to at-or-above) a threshold. The poll rate and exact-alarm option are GLOBAL app settings (Settings → Data Used) shared across every DataUsedTrigger; a single AlarmManager alarm runs while at least one trigger is enabled. For calendar periods the trigger auto re-arms when the period rolls over (e.g. on the billing day). For rolling windows, cooldownMinutes prevents repeat fires (default = period length). Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.
- DayDreamTrigger: Triggers when Daydream (screen saver) starts/stops
- DayTrigger: Triggers on specific day of week or day of month
- DeviceUnlockedTrigger: Triggers when device is unlocked (user present)
- DialNumberTrigger: Triggers when specific number is dialed
- DockTrigger: Triggers when device is docked/undocked
- DrawerOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid drawer is opened or closed
- EmailReceivedTrigger: Triggers when email received matching patterns
- EmptyTrigger: Empty/placeholder trigger. Used as a placeholder when trigger is removed or for triggering via external apps.
- ExternalPowerTrigger: Triggers when device is connected or disconnected from power.
- FailedLoginTrigger: Triggers after failed device unlock attempts
- FileChangedTrigger: Triggers when files are created, modified, or deleted in a folder
- FileOpenedTrigger: Triggers when a file is opened with MacroDroid from another app's Open with list (e.g. tapping a file in a file manager)
- FlipDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is flipped face up/down
- FloatingButtonTrigger: Triggers from floating button overlay. When enabled a floating button will be shown as an overlay on the screen.
- FloatingTextClickedTrigger: Triggers when the user clicks or long clicks a floating text (identified by its id). Fires in addition to any click action configured on the floating text. Useful inside WaitUntilTriggerAction to pause a macro until a floating text is tapped. Provides {floating_text_identifier} magic text. A long click is only detected when the floating text has a long-press action/action block/macro configured, so option 1 or 2 needs such a target on the floating text.
- FloatingTextShownHiddenTrigger: Triggers when a floating text (identified by its id) is shown or hidden. Covers programmatic show/hide, hide all and user dismissal (drag/tap/auto-hide).
- FoldAngleTrigger: Triggers based on device fold state (foldable phones)
- GPSEnabledTrigger: Triggers when GPS/location is toggled
- GeofenceTrigger: Triggers when entering/leaving a geographic area
- GoogleAssistantTrigger: Triggers when Google Assistant command is received
- HeadphonesTrigger: Triggers when headphones are connected or disconnected
- HomeButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when home button is long pressed
- HotspotTrigger: Triggers when WiFi hotspot is enabled/disabled
- HttpServerTrigger: Triggers from local HTTP server requests
- IncomingCallTrigger: Triggers on incoming calls
- IncomingSMSTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is received
- IntentReceivedTrigger: Triggers when a broadcast intent is received from another app
- IpAddressChangeTrigger: Triggers when device IP address changes
- KeyboardOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when the soft keyboard is opened or closed. Requires the accessibility service.
- LightSensorTrigger: Triggers at specific light level threshold
- LocationTrigger: Triggers when entering or exiting a geofence zone. In general GeofenceTrigger is preferred but this is an alternative that does not use Google Play services
- LogcatTrigger: Triggers on Android system logcat output (adb logcat). Not for MacroDroid's internal log (use SystemLogTrigger).
- MacroDroidEnabledTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid is enabled
- MacroDroidIconLongPressShortcutTrigger: Triggers when the user long-presses the MacroDroid app icon and taps a dynamic shortcut
- MacroDroidInitialisedTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid service starts
- MacroEnabledTrigger: Triggers immediately when the macro is enabled
- MacroFinishedTrigger: Triggers when another macro finishes execution. CAUTION - macroId -1 (this macro) makes the macro re-run every time it finishes, looping forever; only use -1 when an endless loop is intended or is prevented via a constraint/variable check or by disabling the trigger or macro while running
- MediaButtonPressedTrigger: Triggers on media button press (headset button)
- MediaButtonV2Trigger: Triggers on specific media button events via notification listener
- MediaTrackChangedTrigger: Triggers when media track changes
- MicrophoneRecordingTrigger: Triggers when any app starts or stops using/recording with the device microphone (Android 7+). If the ADB hack has granted android.permission.DUMP and android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS, the app is identified and {app_name}/{app_package} magic text is available. Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps - requires the ADB hack (android.permission.DUMP + android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS).
- ModeEnterExitTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid mode is entered or exited
- MusicPlayingTrigger: Triggers when music/audio playback starts or stops. By default detects any playback (the app cannot be identified). Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps (e.g. Spotify, YouTube Music) - detected via their media sessions, requires notification access. Set anyAppMediaSession=true to detect playback from any app via media sessions instead (requires notification access).
- NFCStateTrigger: Triggers when NFC state changes
- NFCTrigger: Triggers when NFC tag is scanned
- NetworkRoamingChangedTrigger: Triggers when network roaming state changes
- NetworkTransportChangeTrigger: Triggers when the transport of the active (default) network changes (e.g. Android switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, even if both stay connected). While a VPN is active the transport stays VPN, and a change of the transport beneath the VPN (e.g. Wi-Fi disabled, VPN moves to cellular) also fires. Magic text {network_transport} (new), {network_transport_previous} (old) and {network_transport_underlying} (transport beneath a VPN) contain the fixed values Wi-Fi, Cellular, Ethernet, VPN or None. {network_transport_previous} may additionally contain Other (a transport that is none of the above, e.g. Bluetooth tethering); Other never fires the trigger, so it cannot be selected as a transport to match. Note the magic text value for no network is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no network)'. Does not require location permissions.
- NotificationButtonTrigger: Triggers when notification action button is pressed
- NotificationTrigger: Triggers on notification received/cleared. Use for reacting to messages from any app (WhatsApp, Telegram, etc).
- OrientationTrigger: Triggers when device orientation changes between portrait and landscape
- OutgoingCallTrigger: Triggers on outgoing call
- PhotoTakenTrigger: Triggers when a photo is taken by the camera
- PowerButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when power button is long pressed
- PowerButtonToggleTrigger: Triggers when power button is pressed multiple times quickly
- PriorityModeTrigger: Triggers when Do Not Disturb mode changes
- ProximityTrigger: Triggers on proximity sensor events (near/far/wave)
- QuickSettingsTileTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid quick settings tile is tapped
- RegularIntervalTrigger: Triggers repeatedly at a fixed interval (e.g. "every 30 minutes", "every 2 hours", "every 10 seconds"). Use this for any repeating/recurring interval. m_seconds sets the interval in seconds (e.g. 3600 = every hour). NOT for fixed clock times - use TimerTrigger for "at 7:00 AM
- SMSSentTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is sent
- ScreenContentTrigger: Triggers when specific text appears on screen
- ScreenOnOffTrigger: Triggers when screen turns on or off
- ScreenshotContentTrigger: Triggers when screenshot contains specific text (OCR)
- SensorTrigger: Triggers when a value reported by a chosen device sensor crosses a defined threshold. Edge-triggered - fires once when the value crosses the threshold and re-arms only after the value moves back past the threshold. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion and step detector are not. For multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²), useful for orientation-independent movement detection. The value that fired the trigger is available via the [sensor_value] magic text and the name of the sensor via [sensor_type]. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+. Continuous mode pauses in deep sleep; periodic mode samples via alarms and works with the screen off.
- ShakeDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is shaken (only works when screen is on)
- ShareFileTrigger: Triggers when a file is shared to MacroDroid
- ShareTextTrigger: Triggers when text is shared to MacroDroid
- ShizukuStoppedTrigger: Triggers when the Shizuku service stops working or becomes unavailable (e.g. crashes, is manually stopped, or the binder connection is lost)
- ShortcutTrigger: Triggers from home screen shortcut
- SignalOnOffTrigger: Triggers when cellular signal is gained/lost
- SilentModeTrigger: Triggers when silent/ringer mode changes
- SimChangeTrigger: Triggers when SIM card is changed
- SleepTrigger: Triggers when device enters/exits sleep mode
- SpotifyTrigger: Triggers based on Spotify playback events. Track/song change detection requires this trigger (option=2), not MusicPlayingTrigger.
- StopwatchTrigger: Triggers when a named stopwatch reaches specified time
- SunriseSunsetTrigger: Triggers at sunrise or sunset with optional offset
- SwipeTrigger: Triggers when the user performs a swipe gesture on a swipe handle on the screen edge
- SystemLogTrigger: Triggers when entry appears in MacroDroid's internal system log. Not for Android logcat (use LogcatTrigger). A macro's own log entries cannot re-invoke it while a run started by this trigger is in progress, so a wildcard like * is safe but to record which macro ran it is best placed in a standalone macro matching 'Invoking Macro: *'.
- SystemSettingTrigger: Triggers when system setting changes
- SystemTimeTrigger: Triggers at an absolute system time given as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds or milliseconds). The timestamp can be a fixed value or read from an integer variable; when the variable's value changes the scheduled wakeup is automatically rescheduled. If the timestamp is in the past nothing is scheduled and the trigger will not fire. One-shot - after firing it will not fire again until the variable value changes to a new future timestamp. Use TimerTrigger for clock times and RegularIntervalTrigger for repeating intervals.
- TimerTrigger: Triggers at a fixed clock time on specific days of the week (e.g. "at 7:00 AM on weekdays"). NOT for repeating intervals - use RegularIntervalTrigger for "every X minutes/hours
- ToastTrigger: Triggers when a toast message appears
- UIClickTrigger: Triggers when specific UI element is clicked
- USBTetheringTrigger: Triggers when USB tethering is enabled or disabled
- UsbDeviceConnectionTrigger: Triggers when USB device is connected/disconnected
- VariableTrigger: Triggers when a variable value changes or meets specified conditions
- VolumeButtonTrigger: Triggers on volume button press
- VolumeLongPressTrigger: Triggers when volume button is long pressed (works with screen off). Requires the SET_VOLUME_KEY_LONG_PRESS_LISTENER permission granted via ADB or root. While any macro with this trigger is enabled, MacroDroid intercepts screen-off volume key handling system-wide (standard handling is restored when all such triggers are disabled or removed).
- VpnTrigger: Triggers when VPN connection state changes
- WearOSComplicationClickTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid complication is clicked on a Wear OS watch face
- WeatherTrigger: Triggers based on weather conditions
- WebHook2wayTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL and can return a response to the caller (Firebase-based; Pro version only)
- WebHookTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL (Firebase-based)
- WifiConnectionTrigger: Triggers on WiFi connection state changes
- WidgetPressedTrigger: Triggers from widget button press
- WifiSSIDTrigger: Triggers when specific WiFi network is in/out of range
- WorkProfileTrigger: Triggers when the work profile is enabled or disabled

## ACTIONS
- AccessibilityServiceAction: Enable, disable, or toggle accessibility services
- ActionBlockAction: Invoke/run an action block with input/output variable mapping
- AddCalendarEntryAction: Add an event to the calendar
- AiLlmQueryAction: Query an AI/LLM model with a prompt (supports both on-device Gemini Nano and cloud APIs)
- AmbientDisplayAction: Enable/disable ambient display (always-on display or wake for notifications)
- AndroidShortcutsAction: Perform Android system global actions via accessibility service
- AndroidWearAction: Control Android Wear/Wear OS device from phone
- AnimationOverlayAction: Display animated overlay (Lottie/Giphy/GIF). Only a single animation can be played at any one time.
- AnswerCallAction: Answer an incoming phone call
- ArrayManipulationAction: Manipulate and filter array variables
- AuthenticateUserAction: Require biometric or PIN/password authentication
- BatterySaverAction: Enable/disable battery saver mode
- BlockTouchesAction: Block touch input on screen (enable/disable/toggle)
- BluetoothTetheringAction: Enable/disable Bluetooth tethering
- BreakFromLoopAction: Break out of current loop
- BubbleNotificationAction: Display floating bubble notification overlay
- CameraFlashLightAction: Control camera flashlight/torch
- CameraNotificationCircleAction: Display a notification circle overlay around the camera area with animated gradient colors
- CancelActiveMacroAction: Cancel/stop a running macro
- CaptureNextClickXYAction: Capture coordinates of next user tap into dictionary variable
- CarModeAction: Enable/disable car mode (Android UI mode)
- CheckImageOnScreenAction: Captures a screenshot and checks if a specified reference image is present on the screen using OpenCV template matching. Useful for detecting when a specific button or UI element appears (e.g. in a game). Optionally saves match location and bounds to a dictionary variable so they can be used with a Click action.
- CheckPixelColorAction: Check color of specific pixel on screen
- CheckTextInScreenshotAction: Check for text in screenshot using OCR
- CheckTextOnScreenAction: Check if specific text is visible on screen using accessibility service
- ClearAppDataAction: Clear app data using pm clear command
- ClearCallLogAction: Clear call history entries
- ClearDialogAction: Clear any open MacroDroid dialog
- ClearDictionaryArrayEntryAction: Clear entry from dictionary or array variable
- ClearLogAction: Clear MacroDroid user or system logs
- ClearNotificationsAction: Clear notifications from status bar with filtering options
- ClearVariablesAction: Clear (reset) one or more variables to their empty state (strings "", numbers 0, booleans false), by explicit list or name pattern
- ClipboardAction: Set clipboard text content
- CloseApplicationAction: Force close/kill an application
- ConfigureAppNotificationsAction: Configure app notification settings (enable/disable notifications per app)
- ConfigureWidgetButtonAction: Configure MacroDroid widget button appearance
- ConfirmDialogAction: Show dialog with multiple buttons and optional action blocks
- ConfirmNextAction: Require confirmation before executing the next action
- ConnectivityCheckAction: Check network connectivity by reaching a website
- ContactViaAppAction: Contact someone via specific app using contact data
- ContinueLoopAction: Skip to next iteration of current loop
- ControlMediaAction: Control media playback (play/pause/next/previous/stop)
- CreateChartAction: Create chart image from array data and display or save it
- CustomSceneAction: Display custom scene with UI elements
- DarkThemeAction: Enable/disable/toggle dark theme
- DayDreamAction: Start daydream/screensaver mode
- DeleteVariableAction: Delete one or more variables, by single name, explicit list or name pattern
- DimScreenAction: Add a dimming overlay to reduce screen brightness beyond system limits. This is NOT the same as SetBrightnessAction. Use DimScreenAction when you need to dim/darken the screen (it adds a dark overlay on top). Use SetBrightnessAction only to change the system brightness slider value.
- DisableAppAction: Enable or disable applications using pm command
- DisableCameraAction: Enable/disable device camera via device admin
- DisableCategoryAction: Enable/disable macros in a category
- DisableMacroAction: Enable, disable, or toggle another macro
- DisableMacroDroidAction: Disable MacroDroid completely (stops all macro execution)
- DisableTriggerAction: Enable/disable specific trigger within a macro
- DisplayDensityAction: Change display density (DPI scale percentage)
- EdgeLightingAction: Show animated edge lighting effect around screen borders with gradient colors
- ElseAction: Else branch of if statement
- ElseIfConditionAction: Else If condition check - executes child actions if conditions are met and previous If/ElseIf was false
- ElseIfConfirmedThenAction: Else If with user confirmation - shows dialog and executes child actions if user confirms and previous If/ElseIf was false
- EncryptDecryptTextAction: Encrypt or decrypt text using AES-256
- EndIfAction: End of if/else block
- EndLoopAction: End of loop block - closes a LoopAction
- ExpandCollapseStatusBarAction: Expand or collapse the notification status bar
- ExportMacrosAction: Export all macros to a file (.mdr/.emdr) or store the export JSON in a string variable
- FileOperationAllFilesAction: File operations with all files access (copy/move/delete/create folder/list files)
- FloatingButtonConfigureAction: Configure appearance and behavior of floating button trigger. Use this to show/hide/configure floating buttons (not DisableTriggerAction).
- FloatingTextAction: Show/hide floating text overlay
- FontScaleAction: Change font scale
- ForceLocationUpdateAction: Force immediate location update and optionally store result
- ForceMacroRunAction: Force run another macro
- ForceScreenRotationAction: Force the screen to a specific rotation or cancel forced rotation. On Android 16+ the system ignores orientation requests on large screens (tablets, unfolded foldables), so this action may have no effect on those devices.
- ForwardSMSAction: Forward incoming SMS to another number
- GenerateQRCodeAction: Generate QR code image
- GetCalendarEventsAction: Get calendar events within time range
- GetContactsAction: Get all contacts into a multi-level dictionary keyed by contact display name (sub-keys per contact - Birthday, Phone Number, Address, Email). No filtering is available - every contact is always fetched. The list is sorted alphabetically.
- GetDataUsedAction: Read cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period and store it into a numeric variable. Integer target variables receive the floored whole-unit value; decimal target variables receive the value rounded to 2 decimal places. Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.
- GetInstalledAppsAction: Get list of installed applications
- GetLightLevelAction: Get current light sensor reading
- GetNotificationsAction: Read all notifications currently displayed in the status bar into a dictionary or array variable
- GetTextByViewIdAction: Get text from specific UI element by view ID
- HeadsUpNotificationsAction: Enable/disable heads-up notifications
- HideSceneAction: Hide scene(s) by name with optional pattern matching
- HttpRequestAction: Make an HTTP request
- HttpServerResponseAction: Send response to HTTP server request
- IfConditionAction: Conditional execution (if/then/else)
- IfConfirmedThenAction: Show confirmation dialog and execute child actions if confirmed (parent action)
- ImageDescriptionAction: Get AI description of an image using on-device Gemini
- ImmersiveModeAction: Enable/disable immersive mode (hide status/nav bars)
- ImportMacrosAction: Import macros and action blocks from a MacroDroid export file (.mdr/.emdr) with no user interaction. Settings, global variables and other data in the file are applied as in a manual import. Pair with FileChangedTrigger to auto-import a synced file.
- InputKeyEventAction: Send a key event (simulate key press)
- InvertColoursAction: Invert screen colors
- IterateDictionaryAction: Iterate over dictionary or array entries
- JavaAction: Execute Java/Kotlin code (BeanShell interpreter)
- JavaScriptAction: Execute JavaScript code
- JsonOutputAction: Convert dictionary variable to JSON string
- JsonParseAction: Parse JSON string from variable into dictionary or array variable
- KeepAwakeAction: Keep device awake with wakelock
- KillBackgroundAppAction: Kill background apps to free memory
- LaunchActivityAction: Launch/open an app (a.k.a. Launch App) or a specific Android activity
- LaunchAppActivityAction: Launch specific exported activity from an app
- LaunchHomeScreenAction: Go to the home screen
- LaunchShortcutAction: Launch an Android shortcut created by an app
- LogAction: Write to MacroDroid user log
- LoopAction: Repeat actions a specified number of times, until a condition is met, or for a period of time
- MacroDroidDrawerAction: Configure and control MacroDroid swipe drawer (legacy or custom scene-based drawers)
- MacroDroidNotificationTextAction: Update MacroDroid persistent notification text
- MacroDroidSettingAction: Change MacroDroid app settings
- MakeCallAction: Initiate a phone call
- MessageDialogAction: Display a popup dialog with title and message
- MuteMicrophoneAction: Mute or unmute the device microphone. Uses the standard system microphone mute, which is primarily effective during phone calls and VoIP communication; behaviour outside of a call varies by device.
- MutexAction: Mutex block - only one macro run at a time may execute the actions inside it
- MutexEndAction: End of mutex block - closes a MutexAction and releases the mutex
- NotificationAction: Display a system notification
- NotificationInteractionAction: Interact with notifications
- NotificationReplyAction: Reply to notification or perform notification actions (for messaging apps)
- OCRAction: Perform OCR on image to extract text into array/dictionary variable
- OpenCallLogAction: Open call log screen
- OpenFileAction: Open a file with a specific application, or the system default app for the file type
- OpenLastPhotoAction: Open most recent photo in specified app
- OpenMacroDroidLogAction: Open MacroDroid log screen
- OpenWebPageAction: Open URL in browser or perform HTTP GET request
- OptionDialogAction: Display a dialog with up to 3 button options that can trigger macros or action blocks
- OverlayDialogAction: Display an overlay dialog with customizable content (extends NotificationAction)
- PauseAction: Pause execution for specified time (Wait action)
- PinUnlockAction: Unlock device by entering PIN via accessibility
- PlaySoundAction: Play a sound file or stop playing sounds
- PressBackAction: Simulate pressing the back button
- ProofreadingAction: Proofread text using on-device Google AI (Gemini Nano) to correct spelling and grammar errors
- ReadFileAction: Read contents of a text file into a variable. UTF-8 (with or without BOM) and UTF-16 with BOM are decoded automatically; files that are not valid UTF-8 fall back to the legacy charset of the device locale (e.g. CP949 for Korean Excel CSVs).
- ReadQRCodeAction: Read QR code from image source
- ReadScreenContentsAction: Read all text content from current screen via accessibility
- ReadScreenshotContentsAction: Read text from screenshot using OCR
- ReadSoundLevelAction: Measure the sound level from an audio input (microphone by default) for a set period and save the maximum, average and/or minimum level into number variables. Levels are in dB relative to the maximum input level (dBFS), so 0 dB is the loudest possible value and silence is around -96 dB (louder sounds give values closer to 0). Blocks until the capture period has elapsed and the variables have been set. At least one output variable must be set (users usually only need the maximum). Requires the record audio permission.
- RebootAction: Reboot or power off the device
- RecordMicrophoneAction: Record audio from microphone
- RecordVideoAction: Record video from camera
- RefreshWidgetAction: Force a refresh of a custom (Jetpack Glance) home-screen widget, re-rendering its content with current variable values and magic text. Use to keep non-variable magic text (battery, time, etc.) up to date, since those only refresh when something triggers an update.
- RejectCallAction: Reject/end an incoming or active phone call
- RestoreNotificationsAction: Restore previously cleared notifications
- RewriteTextAction: Rewrite text in a different style using on-device Google AI (Gemini Nano)
- SamsungRoutinesAction: Invoke a Samsung Modes & Routines manual routine (Samsung devices only)
- SayTimeAction: Speak current time aloud using text-to-speech
- ScreenOnAction: Turn screen on or off. The classType is "ScreenOnAction" (not "ScreenOnOffAction").
- SecureSettingsAction: 3rd-party Secure Settings PLUGIN only (com.intangibleobject.securesettings.plugin) - to read/write Android system/secure/global settings use SystemSettingAction instead, NOT this
- SelectionDialogAction: Display a selection dialog with customizable buttons from manual entries or dictionary/array variable
- SendEmailAction: Send email via Gmail or SMTP
- SendIntentAction: Send an Android intent (broadcast, activity, or service)
- SendSMSAction: Send an SMS message
- SensorReadAction: Perform a one-off read of a device sensor and save the result into a variable. Blocks until the sensor is read (or up to 5 seconds). Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion, step detector and heart beat are not. Single-value sensors (light, proximity, pressure, temperature, humidity, step counter, heart rate) save into a decimal variable; multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) save into a dictionary variable with named keys (e.g. x, y, z). The device orientation sensor (type 27) saves value0 = 0 portrait, 1 rotated 90 degrees, 2 upside down, 3 rotated 270 degrees, or -1 when the device is flat; if the driver does not report within 1 second the orientation is derived from the accelerometer. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+ because they require a health permission MacroDroid does not hold - do not use them in macros targeting Android 16+ devices.
- SetAirplaneModeAction: Enable/disable airplane mode
- SetAlarmClockAction: Set, disable, or dismiss an alarm clock
- SetAutoRotateAction: Enable/disable auto screen rotation. classType must include "Set" prefix.
- SetAutoSyncAction: Enable/disable auto sync (background data sync)
- SetBluetoothAction: Enable/disable Bluetooth or connect to/disconnect from audio devices
- SetBrightnessAction: Set the auto brightness mode and/or the screen brightness value. The two are independent - you can set just the auto brightness mode, just the brightness value, or both. At least one of setAutoBrightness or setBrightnessValue must be true.
- SetDataAction: Enable/disable mobile data
- SetDigitalAssistantAction: Change default digital assistant
- SetGPSAction: Enable/disable GPS location
- SetHotspotAction: Enable/disable WiFi hotspot
- SetKeyboardAction: Show keyboard picker to change input method
- SetKeyguardAction: Enable/disable device lock screen (keyguard)
- SetLanguageAction: Change system language
- SetLocationModeAction: Set GPS location services mode (enable/disable location services, requires root or ADB permission)
- SetLocationUpdateRateAction: Set MacroDroid location update frequency
- SetMacroDroidIconAction: Change MacroDroid notification icon
- SetModeAction: Set MacroDroid mode (custom user-defined modes)
- SetNFCAction: Enable/disable/toggle NFC

A MacroDroid macro is composed of three kinds of items:
- TRIGGERS: events that start the macro (e.g. TimeTrigger, BatteryLevelTrigger). Every macro has at least one trigger.

## TRIGGERS
- AccessibilityServiceStateTrigger: Triggers when accessibility service state changes
- ActivityRecognitionTrigger: Triggers based on detected user activity (walking, running, in vehicle, etc.)
- AirplaneModeTrigger: Triggers when airplane mode is enabled or disabled
- AndroidWearTrigger: Triggers from Android Wear/Wear OS events - app button press, watch connected, or watch disconnected
- AppActivityLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when a specific activity (screen) is launched or closed
- AppEnabledTrigger: Triggers when an application is enabled or disabled on the device
- ApplicationInstalledRemovedTrigger: Triggers when an application is installed, updated, or removed
- ApplicationLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when app is launched or closed. There is no separate AppCloseTrigger - use this trigger with m_launched=false to detect app close.
- AssistantActivatedTrigger: Triggers when the device's digital assistant (e.g. Gemini, Google Assistant, Bixby) opens or closes. Detects the assistant window appearing/disappearing - it cannot detect whether the assistant is actively listening. Useful for accessibility, e.g. playing a sound when the assistant opens for visually impaired users. Requires the accessibility service.
- AutoRotateChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-rotate setting changes
- AutoSyncChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-sync setting changes
- BatteryLevelTrigger: Triggers at specific battery level
- BatterySaverTrigger: Triggers when battery saver mode changes
- BatteryTemperatureTrigger: Triggers at specific battery temperature
- BluetoothBeaconTrigger: Triggers when Bluetooth beacon is detected
- BluetoothTrigger: Triggers on Bluetooth connection events
- BootTrigger: Triggers when device boots/restarts
- CalendarTrigger: Triggers based on calendar events
- CallActiveTrigger: Triggers when call becomes active (answered) - monitors both incoming and outgoing calls
- CallEndedTrigger: Triggers when a call ends
- CallMissedTrigger: Triggers when a call is missed. classType is "CallMissedTrigger" not "MissedCallTrigger".
- CameraFlashlightTrigger: Triggers when camera flashlight (torch) state changes
- CameraInUseTrigger: Triggers when camera starts or stops being used by another app
- CellConnectionTypeChangeTrigger: Triggers when the mobile (cellular) data connection type changes, e.g. LTE to 5G. Requires Android 11+. Magic text {cell_connection_type_new} (new) and {cell_connection_type_previous} (old) contain the fixed values 2G, 3G, LTE, 5G NSA, 5G SA or None. 5G NSA (non-standalone, 5G over an LTE core) is how most carriers deliver 5G; 5G SA is pure standalone 5G, so a macro that wants "any 5G" should enable both. None means no mobile data connection (e.g. airplane mode or no signal). Note the magic text value is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no mobile data connection)'. Requires phone state permission.
- CellTowerTrigger: Triggers when in/out of range of specified cell towers, or (anyCellChange=true) whenever the serving cell the phone is connected to changes. In anyCellChange mode no cell tower group is needed and magic text {cell_id_new} and {cell_id_previous} contain the new and previous cell IDs. Changes are not reported during calls or with no signal.
- ClipboardChangeTrigger: Triggers when clipboard content changes
- CustomSceneTrigger: Triggers when a custom scene is shown or dismissed (based on its identifier)
- DarkThemeTrigger: Triggers when dark theme is toggled
- DataOnOffTrigger: Triggers when overall data connectivity changes (WiFi OR mobile) - fires on connect/disconnect of any data connection, NOT specifically on mobile data being toggled
- DataUsedTrigger: Fires when cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period crosses (transitions from below to at-or-above) a threshold. The poll rate and exact-alarm option are GLOBAL app settings (Settings → Data Used) shared across every DataUsedTrigger; a single AlarmManager alarm runs while at least one trigger is enabled. For calendar periods the trigger auto re-arms when the period rolls over (e.g. on the billing day). For rolling windows, cooldownMinutes prevents repeat fires (default = period length). Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.
- DayDreamTrigger: Triggers when Daydream (screen saver) starts/stops
- DayTrigger: Triggers on specific day of week or day of month
- DeviceUnlockedTrigger: Triggers when device is unlocked (user present)
- DialNumberTrigger: Triggers when specific number is dialed
- DockTrigger: Triggers when device is docked/undocked
- DrawerOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid drawer is opened or closed
- EmailReceivedTrigger: Triggers when email received matching patterns
- EmptyTrigger: Empty/placeholder trigger. Used as a placeholder when trigger is removed or for triggering via external apps.
- ExternalPowerTrigger: Triggers when device is connected or disconnected from power.
- FailedLoginTrigger: Triggers after failed device unlock attempts
- FileChangedTrigger: Triggers when files are created, modified, or deleted in a folder
- FileOpenedTrigger: Triggers when a file is opened with MacroDroid from another app's Open with list (e.g. tapping a file in a file manager)
- FlipDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is flipped face up/down
- FloatingButtonTrigger: Triggers from floating button overlay. When enabled a floating button will be shown as an overlay on the screen.
- FloatingTextClickedTrigger: Triggers when the user clicks or long clicks a floating text (identified by its id). Fires in addition to any click action configured on the floating text. Useful inside WaitUntilTriggerAction to pause a macro until a floating text is tapped. Provides {floating_text_identifier} magic text. A long click is only detected when the floating text has a long-press action/action block/macro configured, so option 1 or 2 needs such a target on the floating text.
- FloatingTextShownHiddenTrigger: Triggers when a floating text (identified by its id) is shown or hidden. Covers programmatic show/hide, hide all and user dismissal (drag/tap/auto-hide).
- FoldAngleTrigger: Triggers based on device fold state (foldable phones)
- GPSEnabledTrigger: Triggers when GPS/location is toggled
- GeofenceTrigger: Triggers when entering/leaving a geographic area
- GoogleAssistantTrigger: Triggers when Google Assistant command is received
- HeadphonesTrigger: Triggers when headphones are connected or disconnected
- HomeButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when home button is long pressed
- HotspotTrigger: Triggers when WiFi hotspot is enabled/disabled
- HttpServerTrigger: Triggers from local HTTP server requests
- IncomingCallTrigger: Triggers on incoming calls
- IncomingSMSTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is received
- IntentReceivedTrigger: Triggers when a broadcast intent is received from another app
- IpAddressChangeTrigger: Triggers when device IP address changes
- KeyboardOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when the soft keyboard is opened or closed. Requires the accessibility service.
- LightSensorTrigger: Triggers at specific light level threshold
- LocationTrigger: Triggers when entering or exiting a geofence zone. In general GeofenceTrigger is preferred but this is an alternative that does not use Google Play services
- LogcatTrigger: Triggers on Android system logcat output (adb logcat). Not for MacroDroid's internal log (use SystemLogTrigger).
- MacroDroidEnabledTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid is enabled
- MacroDroidIconLongPressShortcutTrigger: Triggers when the user long-presses the MacroDroid app icon and taps a dynamic shortcut
- MacroDroidInitialisedTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid service starts
- MacroEnabledTrigger: Triggers immediately when the macro is enabled
- MacroFinishedTrigger: Triggers when another macro finishes execution. CAUTION - macroId -1 (this macro) makes the macro re-run every time it finishes, looping forever; only use -1 when an endless loop is intended or is prevented via a constraint/variable check or by disabling the trigger or macro while running
- MediaButtonPressedTrigger: Triggers on media button press (headset button)
- MediaButtonV2Trigger: Triggers on specific media button events via notification listener
- MediaTrackChangedTrigger: Triggers when media track changes
- MicrophoneRecordingTrigger: Triggers when any app starts or stops using/recording with the device microphone (Android 7+). If the ADB hack has granted android.permission.DUMP and android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS, the app is identified and {app_name}/{app_package} magic text is available. Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps - requires the ADB hack (android.permission.DUMP + android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS).
- ModeEnterExitTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid mode is entered or exited
- MusicPlayingTrigger: Triggers when music/audio playback starts or stops. By default detects any playback (the app cannot be identified). Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps (e.g. Spotify, YouTube Music) - detected via their media sessions, requires notification access. Set anyAppMediaSession=true to detect playback from any app via media sessions instead (requires notification access).
- NFCStateTrigger: Triggers when NFC state changes
- NFCTrigger: Triggers when NFC tag is scanned
- NetworkRoamingChangedTrigger: Triggers when network roaming state changes
- NetworkTransportChangeTrigger: Triggers when the transport of the active (default) network changes (e.g. Android switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, even if both stay connected). While a VPN is active the transport stays VPN, and a change of the transport beneath the VPN (e.g. Wi-Fi disabled, VPN moves to cellular) also fires. Magic text {network_transport} (new), {network_transport_previous} (old) and {network_transport_underlying} (transport beneath a VPN) contain the fixed values Wi-Fi, Cellular, Ethernet, VPN or None. {network_transport_previous} may additionally contain Other (a transport that is none of the above, e.g. Bluetooth tethering); Other never fires the trigger, so it cannot be selected as a transport to match. Note the magic text value for no network is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no network)'. Does not require location permissions.
- NotificationButtonTrigger: Triggers when notification action button is pressed
- NotificationTrigger: Triggers on notification received/cleared. Use for reacting to messages from any app (WhatsApp, Telegram, etc).
- OrientationTrigger: Triggers when device orientation changes between portrait and landscape
- OutgoingCallTrigger: Triggers on outgoing call
- PhotoTakenTrigger: Triggers when a photo is taken by the camera
- PowerButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when power button is long pressed
- PowerButtonToggleTrigger: Triggers when power button is pressed multiple times quickly
- PriorityModeTrigger: Triggers when Do Not Disturb mode changes
- ProximityTrigger: Triggers on proximity sensor events (near/far/wave)
- QuickSettingsTileTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid quick settings tile is tapped
- RegularIntervalTrigger: Triggers repeatedly at a fixed interval (e.g. "every 30 minutes", "every 2 hours", "every 10 seconds"). Use this for any repeating/recurring interval. m_seconds sets the interval in seconds (e.g. 3600 = every hour). NOT for fixed clock times - use TimerTrigger for "at 7:00 AM
- SMSSentTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is sent
- ScreenContentTrigger: Triggers when specific text appears on screen
- ScreenOnOffTrigger: Triggers when screen turns on or off
- ScreenshotContentTrigger: Triggers when screenshot contains specific text (OCR)
- SensorTrigger: Triggers when a value reported by a chosen device sensor crosses a defined threshold. Edge-triggered - fires once when the value crosses the threshold and re-arms only after the value moves back past the threshold. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion and step detector are not. For multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²), useful for orientation-independent movement detection. The value that fired the trigger is available via the [sensor_value] magic text and the name of the sensor via [sensor_type]. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+. Continuous mode pauses in deep sleep; periodic mode samples via alarms and works with the screen off.
- ShakeDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is shaken (only works when screen is on)
- ShareFileTrigger: Triggers when a file is shared to MacroDroid
- ShareTextTrigger: Triggers when text is shared to MacroDroid
- ShizukuStoppedTrigger: Triggers when the Shizuku service stops working or becomes unavailable (e.g. crashes, is manually stopped, or the binder connection is lost)
- ShortcutTrigger: Triggers from home screen shortcut
- SignalOnOffTrigger: Triggers when cellular signal is gained/lost
- SilentModeTrigger: Triggers when silent/ringer mode changes
- SimChangeTrigger: Triggers when SIM card is changed
- SleepTrigger: Triggers when device enters/exits sleep mode
- SpotifyTrigger: Triggers based on Spotify playback events. Track/song change detection requires this trigger (option=2), not MusicPlayingTrigger.
- StopwatchTrigger: Triggers when a named stopwatch reaches specified time
- SunriseSunsetTrigger: Triggers at sunrise or sunset with optional offset
- SwipeTrigger: Triggers when the user performs a swipe gesture on a swipe handle on the screen edge
- SystemLogTrigger: Triggers when entry appears in MacroDroid's internal system log. Not for Android logcat (use LogcatTrigger). A macro's own log entries cannot re-invoke it while a run started by this trigger is in progress, so a wildcard like * is safe but to record which macro ran it is best placed in a standalone macro matching 'Invoking Macro: *'.
- SystemSettingTrigger: Triggers when system setting changes
- SystemTimeTrigger: Triggers at an absolute system time given as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds or milliseconds). The timestamp can be a fixed value or read from an integer variable; when the variable's value changes the scheduled wakeup is automatically rescheduled. If the timestamp is in the past nothing is scheduled and the trigger will not fire. One-shot - after firing it will not fire again until the variable value changes to a new future timestamp. Use TimerTrigger for clock times and RegularIntervalTrigger for repeating intervals.
- TimerTrigger: Triggers at a fixed clock time on specific days of the week (e.g. "at 7:00 AM on weekdays"). NOT for repeating intervals - use RegularIntervalTrigger for "every X minutes/hours
- ToastTrigger: Triggers when a toast message appears
- UIClickTrigger: Triggers when specific UI element is clicked
- USBTetheringTrigger: Triggers when USB tethering is enabled or disabled
- UsbDeviceConnectionTrigger: Triggers when USB device is connected/disconnected
- VariableTrigger: Triggers when a variable value changes or meets specified conditions
- VolumeButtonTrigger: Triggers on volume button press
- VolumeLongPressTrigger: Triggers when volume button is long pressed (works with screen off). Requires the SET_VOLUME_KEY_LONG_PRESS_LISTENER permission granted via ADB or root. While any macro with this trigger is enabled, MacroDroid intercepts screen-off volume key handling system-wide (standard handling is restored when all such triggers are disabled or removed).
- VpnTrigger: Triggers when VPN connection state changes
- WearOSComplicationClickTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid complication is clicked on a Wear OS watch face
- WeatherTrigger: Triggers based on weather conditions
- WebHook2wayTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL and can return a response to the caller (Firebase-based; Pro version only)
- WebHookTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL (Firebase-based)
- WifiConnectionTrigger: Triggers on WiFi connection state changes
- WidgetPressedTrigger: Triggers from widget button press
- WifiSSIDTrigger: Triggers when specific WiFi network is in/out of range
- WorkProfileTrigger: Triggers when the work profile is enabled or disabled

You select MacroDroid features that will be needed to build a macro.

A MacroDroid macro is composed of three kinds of items:
- TRIGGERS: events that start the macro (e.g. TimeTrigger, BatteryLevelTrigger). Every macro has at least one trigger.
- ACTIONS: what the macro does when it runs (e.g. SendSmsAction, SetWifiAction).
- CONSTRAINTS: conditions that must be true for the macro/trigger/action to run (e.g. DeviceLockedConstraint, BatteryLevelConstraint).

Below is the full catalog of available features with a short description of each. This catalog is the ONLY source of valid names.

---
## TRIGGERS
- AccessibilityServiceStateTrigger: Triggers when accessibility service state changes
- ActivityRecognitionTrigger: Triggers based on detected user activity (walking, running, in vehicle, etc.)
- AirplaneModeTrigger: Triggers when airplane mode is enabled or disabled
- AndroidWearTrigger: Triggers from Android Wear/Wear OS events - app button press, watch connected, or watch disconnected
- AppActivityLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when a specific activity (screen) is launched or closed
- AppEnabledTrigger: Triggers when an application is enabled or disabled on the device
- ApplicationInstalledRemovedTrigger: Triggers when an application is installed, updated, or removed
- ApplicationLaunchedTrigger: Triggers when app is launched or closed. There is no separate AppCloseTrigger - use this trigger with m_launched=false to detect app close.
- AssistantActivatedTrigger: Triggers when the device's digital assistant (e.g. Gemini, Google Assistant, Bixby) opens or closes. Detects the assistant window appearing/disappearing - it cannot detect whether the assistant is actively listening. Useful for accessibility, e.g. playing a sound when the assistant opens for visually impaired users. Requires the accessibility service.
- AutoRotateChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-rotate setting changes
- AutoSyncChangeTrigger: Triggers when auto-sync setting changes
- BatteryLevelTrigger: Triggers at specific battery level
- BatterySaverTrigger: Triggers when battery saver mode changes
- BatteryTemperatureTrigger: Triggers at specific battery temperature
- BluetoothBeaconTrigger: Triggers when Bluetooth beacon is detected
- BluetoothTrigger: Triggers on Bluetooth connection events
- BootTrigger: Triggers when device boots/restarts
- CalendarTrigger: Triggers based on calendar events
- CallActiveTrigger: Triggers when call becomes active (answered) - monitors both incoming and outgoing calls
- CallEndedTrigger: Triggers when a call ends
- CallMissedTrigger: Triggers when a call is missed. classType is "CallMissedTrigger" not "MissedCallTrigger".
- CameraFlashlightTrigger: Triggers when camera flashlight (torch) state changes
- CameraInUseTrigger: Triggers when camera starts or stops being used by another app
- CellConnectionTypeChangeTrigger: Triggers when the mobile (cellular) data connection type changes, e.g. LTE to 5G. Requires Android 11+. Magic text {cell_connection_type_new} (new) and {cell_connection_type_previous} (old) contain the fixed values 2G, 3G, LTE, 5G NSA, 5G SA or None. 5G NSA (non-standalone, 5G over an LTE core) is how most carriers deliver 5G; 5G SA is pure standalone 5G, so a macro that wants "any 5G" should enable both. None means no mobile data connection (e.g. airplane mode or no signal). Note the magic text value is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no mobile data connection)'. Requires phone state permission.
- CellTowerTrigger: Triggers when in/out of range of specified cell towers, or (anyCellChange=true) whenever the serving cell the phone is connected to changes. In anyCellChange mode no cell tower group is needed and magic text {cell_id_new} and {cell_id_previous} contain the new and previous cell IDs. Changes are not reported during calls or with no signal.
- ClipboardChangeTrigger: Triggers when clipboard content changes
- CustomSceneTrigger: Triggers when a custom scene is shown or dismissed (based on its identifier)
- DarkThemeTrigger: Triggers when dark theme is toggled
- DataOnOffTrigger: Triggers when overall data connectivity changes (WiFi OR mobile) - fires on connect/disconnect of any data connection, NOT specifically on mobile data being toggled
- DataUsedTrigger: Fires when cellular or Wi-Fi data used over a configurable period crosses (transitions from below to at-or-above) a threshold. The poll rate and exact-alarm option are GLOBAL app settings (Settings → Data Used) shared across every DataUsedTrigger; a single AlarmManager alarm runs while at least one trigger is enabled. For calendar periods the trigger auto re-arms when the period rolls over (e.g. on the billing day). For rolling windows, cooldownMinutes prevents repeat fires (default = period length). Requires Usage Access permission. On Android 9 and below, reading cellular usage also requires the Phone (READ_PHONE_STATE) permission.
- DayDreamTrigger: Triggers when Daydream (screen saver) starts/stops
- DayTrigger: Triggers on specific day of week or day of month
- DeviceUnlockedTrigger: Triggers when device is unlocked (user present)
- DialNumberTrigger: Triggers when specific number is dialed
- DockTrigger: Triggers when device is docked/undocked
- DrawerOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid drawer is opened or closed
- EmailReceivedTrigger: Triggers when email received matching patterns
- EmptyTrigger: Empty/placeholder trigger. Used as a placeholder when trigger is removed or for triggering via external apps.
- ExternalPowerTrigger: Triggers when device is connected or disconnected from power.
- FailedLoginTrigger: Triggers after failed device unlock attempts
- FileChangedTrigger: Triggers when files are created, modified, or deleted in a folder
- FileOpenedTrigger: Triggers when a file is opened with MacroDroid from another app's Open with list (e.g. tapping a file in a file manager)
- FlipDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is flipped face up/down
- FloatingButtonTrigger: Triggers from floating button overlay. When enabled a floating button will be shown as an overlay on the screen.
- FloatingTextClickedTrigger: Triggers when the user clicks or long clicks a floating text (identified by its id). Fires in addition to any click action configured on the floating text. Useful inside WaitUntilTriggerAction to pause a macro until a floating text is tapped. Provides {floating_text_identifier} magic text. A long click is only detected when the floating text has a long-press action/action block/macro configured, so option 1 or 2 needs such a target on the floating text.
- FloatingTextShownHiddenTrigger: Triggers when a floating text (identified by its id) is shown or hidden. Covers programmatic show/hide, hide all and user dismissal (drag/tap/auto-hide).
- FoldAngleTrigger: Triggers based on device fold state (foldable phones)
- GPSEnabledTrigger: Triggers when GPS/location is toggled
- GeofenceTrigger: Triggers when entering/leaving a geographic area
- GoogleAssistantTrigger: Triggers when Google Assistant command is received
- HeadphonesTrigger: Triggers when headphones are connected or disconnected
- HomeButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when home button is long pressed
- HotspotTrigger: Triggers when WiFi hotspot is enabled/disabled
- HttpServerTrigger: Triggers from local HTTP server requests
- IncomingCallTrigger: Triggers on incoming calls
- IncomingSMSTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is received
- IntentReceivedTrigger: Triggers when a broadcast intent is received from another app
- IpAddressChangeTrigger: Triggers when device IP address changes
- KeyboardOpenCloseTrigger: Triggers when the soft keyboard is opened or closed. Requires the accessibility service.
- LightSensorTrigger: Triggers at specific light level threshold
- LocationTrigger: Triggers when entering or exiting a geofence zone. In general GeofenceTrigger is preferred but this is an alternative that does not use Google Play services
- LogcatTrigger: Triggers on Android system logcat output (adb logcat). Not for MacroDroid's internal log (use SystemLogTrigger).
- MacroDroidEnabledTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid is enabled
- MacroDroidIconLongPressShortcutTrigger: Triggers when the user long-presses the MacroDroid app icon and taps a dynamic shortcut
- MacroDroidInitialisedTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid service starts
- MacroEnabledTrigger: Triggers immediately when the macro is enabled
- MacroFinishedTrigger: Triggers when another macro finishes execution. CAUTION - macroId -1 (this macro) makes the macro re-run every time it finishes, looping forever; only use -1 when an endless loop is intended or is prevented via a constraint/variable check or by disabling the trigger or macro while running
- MediaButtonPressedTrigger: Triggers on media button press (headset button)
- MediaButtonV2Trigger: Triggers on specific media button events via notification listener
- MediaTrackChangedTrigger: Triggers when media track changes
- MicrophoneRecordingTrigger: Triggers when any app starts or stops using/recording with the device microphone (Android 7+). If the ADB hack has granted android.permission.DUMP and android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS, the app is identified and {app_name}/{app_package} magic text is available. Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps - requires the ADB hack (android.permission.DUMP + android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS).
- ModeEnterExitTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid mode is entered or exited
- MusicPlayingTrigger: Triggers when music/audio playback starts or stops. By default detects any playback (the app cannot be identified). Set selectedAppsOnly=true with packageNameList to only fire for specific apps (e.g. Spotify, YouTube Music) - detected via their media sessions, requires notification access. Set anyAppMediaSession=true to detect playback from any app via media sessions instead (requires notification access).
- NFCStateTrigger: Triggers when NFC state changes
- NFCTrigger: Triggers when NFC tag is scanned
- NetworkRoamingChangedTrigger: Triggers when network roaming state changes
- NetworkTransportChangeTrigger: Triggers when the transport of the active (default) network changes (e.g. Android switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, even if both stay connected). While a VPN is active the transport stays VPN, and a change of the transport beneath the VPN (e.g. Wi-Fi disabled, VPN moves to cellular) also fires. Magic text {network_transport} (new), {network_transport_previous} (old) and {network_transport_underlying} (transport beneath a VPN) contain the fixed values Wi-Fi, Cellular, Ethernet, VPN or None. {network_transport_previous} may additionally contain Other (a transport that is none of the above, e.g. Bluetooth tethering); Other never fires the trigger, so it cannot be selected as a transport to match. Note the magic text value for no network is the bare word None, not the option label 'None (no network)'. Does not require location permissions.
- NotificationButtonTrigger: Triggers when notification action button is pressed
- NotificationTrigger: Triggers on notification received/cleared. Use for reacting to messages from any app (WhatsApp, Telegram, etc).
- OrientationTrigger: Triggers when device orientation changes between portrait and landscape
- OutgoingCallTrigger: Triggers on outgoing call
- PhotoTakenTrigger: Triggers when a photo is taken by the camera
- PowerButtonLongPressTrigger: Triggers when power button is long pressed
- PowerButtonToggleTrigger: Triggers when power button is pressed multiple times quickly
- PriorityModeTrigger: Triggers when Do Not Disturb mode changes
- ProximityTrigger: Triggers on proximity sensor events (near/far/wave)
- QuickSettingsTileTrigger: Triggers when MacroDroid quick settings tile is tapped
- RegularIntervalTrigger: Triggers repeatedly at a fixed interval (e.g. "every 30 minutes", "every 2 hours", "every 10 seconds"). Use this for any repeating/recurring interval. m_seconds sets the interval in seconds (e.g. 3600 = every hour). NOT for fixed clock times - use TimerTrigger for "at 7:00 AM
- SMSSentTrigger: Triggers when an SMS is sent
- ScreenContentTrigger: Triggers when specific text appears on screen
- ScreenOnOffTrigger: Triggers when screen turns on or off
- ScreenshotContentTrigger: Triggers when screenshot contains specific text (OCR)
- SensorTrigger: Triggers when a value reported by a chosen device sensor crosses a defined threshold. Edge-triggered - fires once when the value crosses the threshold and re-arms only after the value moves back past the threshold. Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion and step detector are not. For multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) one component of the reading is tested, using the same component names as SensorReadAction dictionary keys (x, y, z, azimuth, pitch, roll, value0...). 3-axis sensors additionally support componentIndex -2 = magnitude sqrt(x²+y²+z²), useful for orientation-independent movement detection. The value that fired the trigger is available via the [sensor_value] magic text and the name of the sensor via [sensor_type]. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+. Continuous mode pauses in deep sleep; periodic mode samples via alarms and works with the screen off.
- ShakeDeviceTrigger: Triggers when device is shaken (only works when screen is on)
- ShareFileTrigger: Triggers when a file is shared to MacroDroid
- ShareTextTrigger: Triggers when text is shared to MacroDroid
- ShizukuStoppedTrigger: Triggers when the Shizuku service stops working or becomes unavailable (e.g. crashes, is manually stopped, or the binder connection is lost)
- ShortcutTrigger: Triggers from home screen shortcut
- SignalOnOffTrigger: Triggers when cellular signal is gained/lost
- SilentModeTrigger: Triggers when silent/ringer mode changes
- SimChangeTrigger: Triggers when SIM card is changed
- SleepTrigger: Triggers when device enters/exits sleep mode
- SpotifyTrigger: Triggers based on Spotify playback events. Track/song change detection requires this trigger (option=2), not MusicPlayingTrigger.
- StopwatchTrigger: Triggers when a named stopwatch reaches specified time
- SunriseSunsetTrigger: Triggers at sunrise or sunset with optional offset
- SwipeTrigger: Triggers when the user performs a swipe gesture on a swipe handle on the screen edge
- SystemLogTrigger: Triggers when entry appears in MacroDroid's internal system log. Not for Android logcat (use LogcatTrigger). A macro's own log entries cannot re-invoke it while a run started by this trigger is in progress, so a wildcard like * is safe but to record which macro ran it is best placed in a standalone macro matching 'Invoking Macro: *'.
- SystemSettingTrigger: Triggers when system setting changes
- SystemTimeTrigger: Triggers at an absolute system time given as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds or milliseconds). The timestamp can be a fixed value or read from an integer variable; when the variable's value changes the scheduled wakeup is automatically rescheduled. If the timestamp is in the past nothing is scheduled and the trigger will not fire. One-shot - after firing it will not fire again until the variable value changes to a new future timestamp. Use TimerTrigger for clock times and RegularIntervalTrigger for repeating intervals.
- TimerTrigger: Triggers at a fixed clock time on specific days of the week (e.g. "at 7:00 AM on weekdays"). NOT for repeating intervals - use RegularIntervalTrigger for "every X minutes/hours
- ToastTrigger: Triggers when a toast message appears
- UIClickTrigger: Triggers when specific UI element is clicked
- USBTetheringTrigger: Triggers when USB tethering is enabled or disabled
- UsbDeviceConnectionTrigger: Triggers when USB device is connected/disconnected
- VariableTrigger: Triggers when a variable value changes or meets specified conditions
- VolumeButtonTrigger: Triggers on volume button press
- VolumeLongPressTrigger: Triggers when volume button is long pressed (works with screen off). Requires the SET_VOLUME_KEY_LONG_PRESS_LISTENER permission granted via ADB or root. While any macro with this trigger is enabled, MacroDroid intercepts screen-off volume key handling system-wide (standard handling is restored when all such triggers are disabled or removed).
- VpnTrigger: Triggers when VPN connection state changes
- WearOSComplicationClickTrigger: Triggers when a MacroDroid complication is clicked on a Wear OS watch face
- WeatherTrigger: Triggers based on weather conditions
- WebHook2wayTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL and can return a response to the caller (Firebase-based; Pro version only)
- WebHookTrigger: Triggers via cloud webhook URL (Firebase-based)
- WifiConnectionTrigger: Triggers on WiFi connection state changes
- WidgetPressedTrigger: Triggers from widget button press
- WifiSSIDTrigger: Triggers when specific WiFi network is in/out of range
- WorkProfileTrigger: Triggers when the work profile is enabled or disabled

- SensorReadAction: Perform a one-off read of a device sensor and save the result into a variable. Blocks until the sensor is read (or up to 5 seconds). Only sensors that can be sampled in real time are supported (continuous and on-change sensors); one-shot/trigger sensors such as significant motion, step detector and heart beat are not. Single-value sensors (light, proximity, pressure, temperature, humidity, step counter, heart rate) save into a decimal variable; multi-value sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, gravity, rotation vector, orientation) save into a dictionary variable with named keys (e.g. x, y, z). The device orientation sensor (type 27) saves value0 = 0 portrait, 1 rotated 90 degrees, 2 upside down, 3 rotated 270 degrees, or -1 when the device is flat; if the driver does not report within 1 second the orientation is derived from the accelerometer. Body sensors (heart rate 21, low latency off-body detect 34) are unavailable on Android 16+ because they require a health permission MacroDroid does not hold - do not use them in macros targeting Android 16+ devices.
